maintenance_cases.status: engineered deterministic mechanism trace; not model performance
maintenance_cases.description: Eight identical event steps for every schedule, three review attempts each, and at most two governing records inspected per review. Coverage and dependency machinery are identical. Review timing changes source exposure; interrupted attempts consume budget.

conditions.schedule: governing dependent change or explicitly detected incorporation gap

events.note: Notification based only on the dependency map misses this governing change. The evaluator still measures actual source-versus-view lag.
The shared audit detects K602 revision mismatch, records its known gap, and restores the omitted dependency before scheduled review.
Any schedule reviewing here reads current sources and writes a temporary candidate, but interruption prevents atomic current.json replacement. Do not advance committed coverage.

shared_mechanics.notification: Mark current.json dirty only when a changed governing source ID is in the current dependency map. Never treat an unchanged dirty flag as certified correctness.
shared_mechanics.audit: At audit checkpoints compare each review_source_id available revision with committed view.coverage; record sorted known_gaps and dirty. Repair dependency mapping from the retained declaration, not a model guess.
shared_mechanics.review: Inspect the same review_source_ids under the per-review cap. Build candidate fields from available governing source fields and candidate coverage from inspected versions. Clear dirty and gaps only after successful atomic commit. An interrupted review leaves committed fields and coverage unchanged and retains gaps.
shared_mechanics.safe_reader_rule: A dirty view or nonempty known_gaps requires source expansion or a blocked continuation. This simulation records such a warning, not whether an LLM obeys it.
shared_mechanics.stopping_rule: Never exceed three review attempts; all eight source replay steps still run. No final free cleanup.

limitations: Schedules have equal attempt caps and update replay counts, but different reviewed source-version exposure. This is a whole-policy effect, not timing alone.
The dependency omission is not automatically repaired by triggering; shared explicit audits expose it.
Known gaps are warnings, not proof that downstream readers act safely.
Prescribed deterministic projection repair does not measure LLM correctness or maintenance competence.
